title: Installer stuck at "Closing Power Toys application"
author: daniporr
summary: The 0.100.0 user installer hangs on a clean Windows Sandbox while running the PowerToys termination package even though PowerToys is not installed.
next_action: Track and validate PR #48658 against a clean Sandbox install instead of opening another implementation.

confidence.rationale: The open PR explicitly names and changes the exact failing installer path.

judgment.rationale: Open PR #48658 directly implements the reported fresh-install guard and termination-script fallback, so a competing fix plan would duplicate active work.
evidence: The issue reproduces on a clean Windows Sandbox at `Closing Power Toys application`.
The PR author linked #48658 and described skipping the termination package when no installed version is detected.
PR #48658 is currently open and changes PowerToys.wxs plus terminate_powertoys.cmd for this exact scenario.
judgment.recommended_action: Track and validate PR #48658 against a clean Sandbox install instead of opening another implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR #48658 directly covers the clean-install hang and termination retry path.

issue_context.summary: The 0.100.0 user installer hangs on a clean Windows Sandbox while running the PowerToys termination package even though PowerToys is not installed.
known_information: The affected installer is PowerToysUserSetup 0.100.0 x64.
Ending the `Terminates processes` task allows installation to finish.
PR #48658 is open and not merged.
inferences: The bootstrapper launches a termination helper on fresh install and waits indefinitely when no PowerToys process exists.
issue_context.analysis: The active PR targets both scheduling and script robustness; the useful next step is review and clean-environment validation.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue discussion and workaround.
Fetched live PR #48658 state, description, and changed-file list.

actions.label: Track fix in PR 48658

comment.body: PR #48658 directly addresses this clean-install hang by skipping the `TerminatePowerToys` package when no existing PowerToys installation is detected and by making `terminate_powertoys.cmd` exit promptly when no process is running. Please validate that PR in a fresh Windows Sandbox; this issue should remain linked to that implementation rather than starting a competing fix.
